CASE STUDY — DOCTOR EN CASA

Telemedicine for Peru,
in Spanish.

Doctor En Casa brings the doctor to the patient — find a doctor in your network, check the specialty, and book a free video appointment. I designed the website end to end, in Spanish, for patients and providers across Peru — from a blank page to a shipped site, then stayed with the developers until what went live matched the designs.

CLIENTDoctor En Casa
WHAT I DIDWebsite UX + UI
YEAR2020
PLATFORMWebsite
01 / THE WEBSITE

The whole site.
Top to bottom.

Seven full-page captures — the homepage in three versions, and the four pages inside it. Tap any page to see it bigger.

02 / THE BRIEF

Seeing a doctor meant
phone calls and waiting rooms.

Patients didn’t know which specialist they needed, what a video consultation would cost, or whether the doctor was real. The site had to make booking feel easy — in Spanish, for patients and providers alike.

The problem

Booking a doctor in Peru meant phone calls, waiting rooms and guesswork. Which specialist do you need? What will a video consultation cost? Is the doctor on the other end real? Most people gave up before they ever got an appointment.

Doctor En Casa removed the friction: find a doctor in your network, check the specialty, book a free video appointment — no downloads, no waiting room. My job was to make that feel obvious from the first screen, in Spanish, for two very different audiences: patients who need care, and providers who offer it.

What I did

  • Homepage + doctor search — specialty and date, above the fold
  • Eight specialties as icon tiles — one tap to the right doctor
  • Patient and provider pages — each audience gets its own door
  • Pricing, explained in plain Spanish — FAQs and a commission table in soles
  • About page — the mission: telemedicine for all of Peru
  • Two visual directions — blue and green, tested side by side
03 / FROM WIREFRAME TO SCREEN

Grey boxes first.
Colour came second.

Every key page was sketched and tested as a wireframe before a single colour went in. The layout had to work in grey — or it didn’t work at all.

The wireframes settled three decisions early: the search is the hero — specialty and date, not a headline. Patients and providers get separate doors, not one shared page. And pricing is a page of plain questions, not a sales pitch.

04 / WHAT THE RESEARCH SHOWED

Tested with real people.
Changed by what they did.

Before the final UI, I ran the flows past first-time users and watched where they hesitated. Four findings shaped the finished pages.

01

The search is the homepage

In testing, first-time visitors went straight to the two search fields — specialty and date — before touching the navigation. So the hero is a search box with a photo behind it, not a headline with a button. Booking starts the moment the page loads.

02

Two doors, not one

Patients and providers wanted different things, so the site gives them separate doors. In testing, mixing the two audiences on one page confused both — the split into a doctor card and a patient card let each side see itself in the first five seconds.

03

Price answers the fear first

Cost was the first question every patient asked. The Precios page leads with plain questions — “¿Cuánto cuesta un médico en línea?” — and a commission table in soles (20% / 10% / 5%), so the money conversation happens on the page instead of on a phone call.

04

Specialties you can recognise

Eight specialties as icon tiles, not a dropdown list. In testing, people found their specialty from the icon before reading the label — Medicina Interna, Ginecología, Pediatría, Dermatología, Psiquiatría, Oftalmología, Otorrinolaringología, Gastroenterología. One glance, one tap.

05 / HOW I WORK

From a blank page
to a shipped product.

I don’t just design screens. Every project runs through the same four phases — and I stay with it until what ships matches what was designed.

01

Discover

Research first. Stakeholder calls, market and competitor analysis, and real user conversations — so the design solves the right problem, not the loudest one.

02

Define

Personas, journeys and flows. The structure gets decided here, on paper, before anything visual exists.

03

Design

Wireframes first, then high fidelity. Low-fi wireframes tested early, then pixel-perfect UI — validated with A/B tests, user testing and usability sessions.

04

Deliver

Handover is not the end. Annotated designs, walkthroughs with the developers, build reviews against the designs — and continuous support after launch.
